history.period: ~11th century CE (attributed); inscriptions dated 1038, 1044 and 1045 AD
history.summary: A Shiva temple in Chola architectural style about 200 m from Kanyakumari railway station, traditionally said to have been built by Raja Raja Chola. It holds 16 inscriptions from the 11th century and is famed for the 1008-conch abhishekam on Purattasi Thiruvathirai. Devotees bathe at Triveni Sangam before worshipping Bhairava here. (VERIFY: the Raja Raja Chola construction claim is traditional attribution; only the inscriptions independently confirm an 11th-century date. Opening hours differ across sources.)

name: Guganathaswamy Temple
town_description: Kanyakumari is the town at the southernmost tip of mainland India, in Kanyakumari district of Tamil Nadu, where the Bay of Bengal, Arabian Sea and Indian Ocean meet at the Triveni Sangam. A historic pilgrimage centre since at least the 1st century CE, it draws devotees to the Kumari Amman temple and tourists for its sunrise/sunset views, the Vivekananda Rock Memorial and the Thiruvalluvar statue.

travel.airport: Thiruvananthapuram International Airport, about 100 km (verify exact distance)
travel.railway: Kanyakumari railway station, about 200 m from the temple
travel.road: On NH 44; town buses, taxis and autos connect the railway station and bus stand to the temple

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Purattasi (Sep-Oct) for the 1008-conch abhishekam
visitor_information.opening_hours: Approx 6:00-11:15 AM and 5:00-8:45 PM (VERIFY: also reported 5:30 AM-12:30 PM and 5:00-8:00 PM)
